title: Minimax Dose-Response Estimation When the Treatment Density Is Rougher Than the Outcome Regression
banked_reason: The promised sharp same-class minimax exponent (and any necessary logarithm) is replaced by an open proposed estimator/risk inequality; the delivered bracket does not determine that frontier.
gap_reasons: The promised sharp same-class minimax exponent (and any necessary logarithm) is replaced by an open proposed estimator/risk inequality; the delivered bracket does not determine that frontier.
The two-window multiscale risk inequality, estimated normalization, design weights, higher-order variance, absence of a logarithm, and exclusion of stronger lower families remain open.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a legal normalized cusp-density mixture lower bound of order n^(-8/39) and an observable window-reduction upper bound of order n^(-1/5). The proposed two-window correction was not constructed: its population drift, estimated normalization, design weights, and higher-order variance remain open. The field-tier sharp exponent and logarithm therefore could not be delivered; a future solver may retry the explicit one-parent drift test before attempting the global estimator.
tldr: The fixed-dose mean is identified, but the treatment density is rougher in dose than the outcome regression, so the one-window higher-order analysis does not determine the full-class frontier. The proposal establishes a legal normalized two-prior lower experiment at MSE order \(n^{-8/39}\), an observable same-class upper benchmark at \(n^{-1/5}\), and a strict class-separation result showing why the neighboring dose-Lipschitz candidate does not transfer. Its central open question is whether a normalized two-window multiscale correction attains \(n^{-8/39}\) without a logarithm; the one-parent population-drift identity is the early kill test.
gap: Bonvini and Kennedy prove estimator-specific conditional upper bounds and explicitly leave a tight minimax lower bound open. Their displayed one-window bias tracks the rougher dose nuisance, and neither their theorem nor later general-treatment work supplies an all-estimator converse or a full-class observable match when the treatment density is only dose-Hölder \(1/4\).
fill: The project uses an exactly normalized unequal-window mixture for the converse, an observable missing-response reduction for a benchmark upper bound, and a two-window parent-child correction handle whose drift and higher-order variance would close the remaining polynomial gap.
